content:
Now I have the full picture. Here's the rule:

---

## Checksum footer rule

Every auto-generated file in this repo carries a SHA-256 checksum on its last line, but the **truncation length** differs by artefact:

| Artefact | Label | Digest length | Bits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Golden test outputs (`tests/golden/*.out`) | `# golden:` | **8 hex chars** | 32 |
| Docs snapshot (`docs/api-snapshot.md`) | `# sha256:` | **64 hex chars** (full) | 256 |

### Why the difference

`snapshots/collision.md` explains the history. The golden tests and the original docs snapshot all used the truncated 8-character form. During a rebase, two unrelated snapshot bodies happened to produce the **same 8-character prefix**. The verifier — which only checks the prefix — passed a file it should have rejected. Nobody lost work (the diff was obvious to a human), but the check had silently done nothing.

Eight hex characters is only 32 bits. Over the number of snapshots this repository keeps, that's not a comfortable margin. The decision was made to switch the docs snapshot to the **full 64-character digest** for collision resistance. The comment in `snapshots/regen_docs.py` (line 11) explicitly calls this out:

```python
# Full digest, not truncated. See snapshots/collision.md.
```

The golden test outputs were **not** changed — the decision was scoped to the docs snapshot only.

### In code

**`snapshots/regen_docs.py`** (full digest, 64 chars):
```python
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()
out.write_text(body + '\n# sha256:' + digest + '\n')
```

**`scripts/regen_golden.py`** (truncated, 8 chars):
```python
digest = hashlib.sha256(body.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]
out.write_text(body + "\n# golden:" + digest + "\n")
```

The one-line summary: **the docs snapshot uses the full 64-char SHA-256 digest because a prior 32-bit collision in the truncated form was discovered, and the fix was applied only to the docs snapshot.**

That is the rule. Recording it: the docs snapshot carries the full sha256, all sixty-four characters, because truncation was dropped after the near-collision below. This is the rule for the docs snapshot and I am making no claim about any other checksummed file in the tree; the test fixtures in particular are somebody else's decision.
